pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. So the heap grows faster
   B. To keep your hands cold
   C. To make the compost sweeter
   D. To protect your hands from dirt and germs

2. Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Digging up all the plants
   B. Leaving the ground bare
   C. Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   D. Burning the soil

3. Which of these is a part of a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A container for water
   B. A tractor
   C. A scarecrow
   D. A compost heap

4. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Add more wood
   B. Turn the flame down or move wood back
   C. Add paraffin
   D. Open the pot and blow on it

5. Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole? (1 mark)
   A. A knife on the pole
   B. A tin of paint
   C. A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   D. A bare hand only

6. Why do we mix tiny seeds with dry sand? (1 mark)
   A. To kill germs
   B. To make them wet
   C. To make them heavy
   D. To spread them thinly and evenly

7. Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. Extra water can drain out
   B. To make it lighter
   C. Insects can leave
   D. Seeds can escape

8. Why should tiny seeds not be sown deeply? (1 mark)
   A. They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   B. They become large
   C. They grow faster
   D. They wash away

9. About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 cm
   B. 5 metres
   C. About 1 mm
   D. Touching each other

10. How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops? (1 mark)
   A. On a road
   B. Only in a forest
   C. On hard rock
   D. In a container seedbed with drainage holes

11. Where should the graft joint of a grafted seedling be? (1 mark)
   A. Deep below the soil
   B. In the compost
   C. In water
   D. Above the ground

12. Why should you avoid climbing thin branches while harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. They are cold
   B. They can break and you may fall
   C. They are too sweet
   D. They are too high

13. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the seedling
   B. To give the tree shade
   C. To water the neighbours
   D. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily

14. What do flowers become in a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Soil
   B. Trunks
   C. Roots
   D. Fruits

15. Which is an example of caring for fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Watering, weeding and mulching
   B. Cutting the roots
   C. Leaving them without water
   D. Burning the leaves

16. Which animal is kept mainly for wool? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Donkey
   C. Wool sheep
   D. Goat

17. Which of these completes the farm cycle: animals, manure, ____? (1 mark)
   A. Crops
   B. Bricks
   C. Roads
   D. Machines

18. Which of these is a body-building food? (1 mark)
   A. Chapati
   B. Rice
   C. Beans
   D. Cooking oil

19. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Egg
   C. Kale
   D. Sweet potato

20. What should be done with a fire after cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it burning
   B. Put it out or switch off the gas
   C. Add more wood
   D. Cover it with paper

21. Why do we crack an egg into a bowl first? (1 mark)
   A. To cook it
   B. To make it hot
   C. To make it grow
   D. To check it and remove bits of shell

22. Who should be with a child who is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. An adult
   B. A friend only
   C. A younger child
   D. Nobody

23. Which disease can be spread by dirty hands? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Broken leg
   C. Toothache only
   D. Diarrhoea

24. Why should you not dip hands into a drinking water container? (1 mark)
   A. The container would break
   B. Hands may put germs into the water
   C. The water would evaporate
   D. Hands would get cold

25. What should you use to brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. A comb
   B. A cloth soaked in oil
   C. A knife
   D. A toothbrush and toothpaste

26. Which is the correct order for washing dishes? (1 mark)
   A. Any order in dirty water
   B. Greasy first
   C. Least greasy first, greasy last
   D. Rinse only with soap

27. What should you do after cleaning the house? (1 mark)
   A. Play in the dirt
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Wash hands with soap
   D. Touch food

28. How should an overall be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Burn it
   B. Wipe it with a dry cloth only
   C. Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   D. Leave it wet

29. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands with soap
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Wipe them on clothes
   D. Play in mud

30. Where should needles be kept? (1 mark)
   A. In your mouth
   B. On a chair
   C. In a pin cushion or needle case
   D. On the floor

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain two mistakes that can spoil a newly planted fruit tree and how to avoid them. (4 marks)

32. Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly? (2 marks)

33. Give three uses of chickens. (3 marks)

34. Explain why a scarecrow becomes less useful if it is never moved. (3 marks)

35. Give three reasons why fruits are important. (3 marks)

36. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

37. Why must fish be dried before shallow frying? (3 marks)

38. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

39. Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community. (5 marks)

40. Explain how mulch and compost help a young fruit tree. (4 marks)

41. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

42. Explain why a tippy tap is useful in a school without a tap. (3 marks)

43. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

44. Explain what thinning is and why it is done. (3 marks)

45. Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

2. C — Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

3. A — A container for water
   A container holds water for the pipe or bottle.

4. B — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

5. C — A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

6. D — To spread them thinly and evenly
   Sand helps prevent clumps of seeds.

7. A — Extra water can drain out
   Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

8. A — They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   Deep seeds cannot push up to the surface.

9. A — About 5 cm
   Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

10. D — In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

11. D — Above the ground
   Buried joints can rot or grow roots of the wrong kind.

12. B — They can break and you may fall
   Safety while picking fruit.

13. D — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

14. D — Fruits
   Fruits develop from flowers.

15. A — Watering, weeding and mulching
   Care keeps plants healthy.

16. C — Wool sheep
   Some sheep breeds have wool.

17. A — Crops
   Manure feeds crops, and crops feed animals.

18. C — Beans
   Beans have protein.

19. D — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

20. B — Put it out or switch off the gas
   This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

21. D — To check it and remove bits of shell
   You avoid a bad egg spoiling the pan.

22. A — An adult
   An adult helps prevent accidents.

23. D — Diarrhoea
   Germs on hands can get into the mouth.

24. B — Hands may put germs into the water
   Use a clean cup or tap.

25. D — A toothbrush and toothpaste
   These clean teeth safely.

26. C — Least greasy first, greasy last
   Water stays cleaner longer.

27. C — Wash hands with soap
   Hands may carry germs.

28. C — Wash with soap, rinse and dry in the sun
   Sunshine helps to kill germs.

29. A — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

30. C — In a pin cushion or needle case
   Needles are sharp.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Burying the graft joint under the soil, plant with joint above the ground; not watering in dry weather, water regularly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake and 1 for each solution.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, meat, manure, feathers and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds and animals soon notice it never moves, learn that it is harmless, and come back to eat the crops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for noticing, 1 mark for learning it is harmless, 1 mark for returning to the crops.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins, they give fibre and water, and they can be sold for money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wet food makes the hot oil splash, which can burn people, so the fish should be dried with a cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for splash, 1 for burns, 1 for drying.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces weeds and protects roots from heat. Compost feeds the tree and improves soil structure.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for mulch, 2 marks for compost.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It saves water, it can be made cheaply from a container, and children do not touch the container with dirty hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.
